solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good American, that woman who oozes enthusiasm?

definitions.note: the clue words describe a person, so the answer is a noun naming someone who gushes

parts.note: US stands for the United States, so American
a female person referred to as her

explanation.surface: An admiring remark about a kind American lady who is wildly enthusiastic about everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is informal for an effusive person who pours out praise and excitement without restraint.

clue.text: James makes a mistake, we hear, getting tunics

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver the words are to be spoken and matched by sound

parts.note: Jim is short for James and slips means makes a mistake

explanation.surface: A boy called James blunders while picking up school clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Gymslips are sleeveless tunics once worn by British schoolgirls for PE and as uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymslips are a type of sleeveless pinafore dress, a tunic worn as British school uniform.

clue.text: Sort out squats? The rebels don't like that

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the established order that rebels oppose

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange or reorder, so the following letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Squatters are evicted; rebellious types disapprove of such action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort out' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'Sort' alone is the anagram signal and 'out' is fodder alongside squats.
explanation.definitionFit: The existing state of affairs is what rebels want overturned, making the established arrangement their target.

clue.text: Woman from Spain that's upset everyone

parts.note: E is the international vehicle registration code for Spain

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so these letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman has managed to offend everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a female given name, a typical crossword way of clueing a woman.

clue.text: Cast came first and laughed

parts.note: to cast is to throw or chuck
led means was in front, came first

explanation.surface: A theatre company finished top of the competition and laughed with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests actors; here it is the verb meaning to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuckled means gave a quiet, suppressed laugh, so it is a near synonym.

clue.text: Those horrible cheers going up — a tricky situation

indicators.note: horrible suggests something mangled, so the letters of the preceding word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as fodder

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you, as is cheers

explanation.surface: Nasty jeers rise from the crowd, putting someone in an awkward spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges THOSE to HOTSE; 'going up' turns TA (British for thanks, like cheers) into AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the hot seat idiomatically means being in an uncomfortable position under pressure.

clue.text: Decision-making groups cost me with time wasted

indicators.note: wasted suggests ruined or broken up, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that bodies making decisions have squandered their hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Committees are bodies of people appointed to deliberate and reach decisions on matters.

clue.text: French student heading off to join English bank

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: élève is French for a pupil or student

explanation.surface: A student from France sets off to work for an English financial institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks financial but means a river embankment.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee is an embankment built along a river to stop flooding, a type of bank.

clue.text: Member of university staff had to be present

parts.note: a don is a lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge
had in the sense of ate a meal

explanation.surface: An academic was obliged to attend some occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be present' reads as attendance; 'present' is the verb to give.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give something as a gift, which is what presenting means as a verb.

clue.text: Authorisation for each American university

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Each US college needs its own official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit is an official document granting permission, which is an authorisation.

clue.text: This writer is resting in a street, being most miserable

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: in says one set of letters goes inside another

parts.note: a, then ST, the abbreviation for street
lies as in reclines at rest

explanation.surface: The writer lounges in the road feeling thoroughly wretched.
explanation.definitionFit: Measliest is the superlative of measly, meaning paltry or contemptibly small and mean.

clue.text: The old woman, French wine expert

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old woman
vin is the French word for wine

explanation.surface: A mother revealed to be a connoisseur of French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expert' looks like a description of the woman; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A maven (also spelt mavin) is a connoisseur or authority, from Yiddish.

clue.text: Flashy couple left, heading back

indicators.note: heading back means going in reverse, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: a duo is a pair or couple

explanation.surface: A showy pair departed, then returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud describes clothes or colours that are garish and showy, attracting attention.

clue.text: Inept men involved in modern technology showing no remorse

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other piece

parts.note: IT is information technology

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Clumsy blokes working in tech are not sorry at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Impenitent means not repentant, feeling no regret for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Mother goddess having a sort of appeal in African country

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: having means holding something within

parts.note: Urania is the Greek muse of astronomy, a divine figure
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A maternal deity with charm turns up in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Mauritania is a country in north-west Africa on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Very good designer, zesty

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, very good
Mary Quant was the British fashion designer credited with the miniskirt

explanation.surface: Praise for a fashion designer whose work is lively and sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (short for pious) is a crossword staple for very good.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquant means pleasantly sharp or spicy, with a tangy, zesty flavour.

clue.text: Little desire they must have for that fellow

indicators.note: must have says the word is to receive a new piece
for says one piece stands in place of the other

parts.note: he refers to a man
an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: A small craving is what they require for that man.
explanation.definitionFit: Titchy is British informal for very small or tiny.

clue.text: Husband, terrible nerd and liar who won't compromise?

definitions.note: the clue words describe a person, so they stand for a noun

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A husband who is an awful geek and a fibber refuses to give ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner is a person who holds rigid, uncompromising views.

clue.text: Deviously or possibly honestly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A question of whether something was done dishonestly or honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets honesty against deceit, the anagram turning one into the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the sly is an idiom for doing it secretly or underhandedly.

clue.text: Firm supports for occupants of snake pit?

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
bras are supportive underwear

explanation.surface: Company props for whoever lives in a pit full of reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobras are venomous snakes, the sort one would find in a snake pit.

clue.text: Put up with terrible host, entertaining Scotsman?

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest inside
terrible signals the letters are mangled

parts.note: Mac, from the Scots surname prefix, is a nickname for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A dreadful host has a Scottish guest to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is idiomatically to tolerate or endure it.

clue.text: Install something wicked outside show

indicators.note: outside says one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a sin is a wicked act
to wear is to display or show, as in wearing a smile

explanation.surface: Fitting something evil around a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear in is to install someone in office by administering an oath.

clue.text: Padre's animated, being saved

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest is excited at being rescued from danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Spared means saved or kept from harm or destruction.

clue.text: What sounds like tea comes here — something to eat

definitions.text: What sounds like tea comes here
definitions.meaning: the letter T, which is said like tea
British informal word for dessert, the course after the main one

explanation.surface: A riddle about where tea fits and what is then served.
explanation.walkthrough: Afters is British slang for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Read cryptically, the letter T lies after S; the word also means the dessert course.

clue.text: Operative finds something oily in Cornish river

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England
unction is anointing with oil, or an ointment

explanation.surface: A worker discovers an oil slick in a river in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Functional means working or in operation, the same as operative.

clue.text: Like a hopeless situation currently at home

parts.note: now means at present
in means at home

explanation.surface: The current state of a doomed situation is staying put at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where any outcome is bad, so it is hopeless.

clue.text: Be loath, oddly, to offer nonsense

indicators.note: oddly says to take the odd-numbered letters of the words

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to talk rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah is informal for meaningless or empty talk, i.e. rubbish.

clue.text: Princess featured in Equestrian News?

indicators.note: featured in says the letters appear within these words

explanation.surface: A royal turns up in a horse-riding publication.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Anne, the Princess Royal, is a keen equestrian who rode at the 1976 Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is the Princess Royal, daughter of Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: King hated winter to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A monarch disliked the cold season somewhat.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin was a seventh-century king of Northumbria, a named example of a king.

clue.text: A group of English hills or Italian mountains

parts.note: the Pennines are a range of hills in northern England

explanation.surface: A choice between English uplands and Italian peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain range running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: Seek a tan, being ashen but changing

indicators.note: changing signals that the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A pale person tries to get some colour, though altering their complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: To sunbathe is to lie in the sun in order to get brown skin.

clue.text: How lover is regarded, costing a lot of money

definitions.meaning: a lover is held with great affection, much loved
at a high price, as in paying heavily for something

explanation.surface: Romance that proves expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means with deep affection and also at great cost, as in paid a high price.
